summary: Seitatsu Matsunami was a scholar in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held posts as an assistant at the University of Tokyo and as a professor at Taisho University (attested 1992).

Seizan Yanagida (1922–2006) specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He studied at Hanazono, Otani, and Kyoto universities under Kaiten Nukariya and Shin'ichi Hisamatsu, later serving on faculties at Hanazono, Kyoto, and Chubu universities.
Sen Wang (1912–1991) was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Peking University (~1932–1936) and served as a professor at Minzu University of China (~1952–1978).

Senarat Wijayasundara is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. In 1999, he was attested as a teacher at the University of Kelaniya and a visiting lecturer at the Buddhist and Pali College of Singapore.
Senarath Paranavitana (1896–1972) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He succeeded Don Martino de Zilva Wickremasinghe and held a post at Leiden University (~1936–1937).

Senchu Murano (1908–2000) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1929–1933) and the University of Washington (~1934–1938). He served as a professor at Rissho University from around 1957 to 1979.

Sengaku Mayeda (1931–2026) specialized in Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. Educated at the University of Tokyo and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, he held faculty posts at Pennsylvania, Tokyo, and Musashino University.

Senkyo Sakawa (born 1937) works in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. After studying at Rissho University (graduated 1965), he served there as professor of Buddhist studies (attested 1981–1985) and professor emeritus (attested 2026).

Senmyo Naniwa works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a PhD from Savitribai Phule Pune University, studying under Genjun Sasaki, M. G. Dhadphale, J. R. Joshi, and P. V. Bapat, and served as professor at Bukkyo University (attested 2005).
Sensho Kimura (born 1943) is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Otani University (~1963–1971) and later served there as a professor from around 1989 to 2014.

Sensho Murakami (1851–1929) worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at Otani and Toyo universities under Yukitada Takeda, Ryomon, and Gokan Unyei, later serving on the faculties of Tokyo Imperial University, Toyo University, and Otani University.
Sentaro Sawamura (1884–1930) specialized in history, archaeology, and Japanology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1908–1911) and later held an academic post there from around 1921 until 1930.

Seok-hyeong Kim (born 1904) specialized in religious studies and Buddhist studies. Educated at Taisho University, he held posts as a part-time lecturer at Seoul National University and as a professor at Dongguk University.

Seong-Uk Kim is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who completed his doctoral studies under Robert E. Buswell Jr. In 2026, he was attested as Cho Associate Professor in Korean Culture and Religion at Columbia University.
Ser Kha Chödrak studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Sergey Malov (1880–1957) was a linguist and scholar of Iranian, Central Asian, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kazan Theological Academy and Saint Petersburg University under Nikolai Katanov, he held posts at Kazan Federal University and Saint Petersburg State University.

Sergey Oldenburg (1863–1934) was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Ivan Minayev. He served as professor at Saint Petersburg State University and director of the Asiatic Museum.

Serinity Young (1944–2020) specialized in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under Alex Wayman and held posts at the American Museum of Natural History and Southern Methodist University (attested 2000).
Sesso Oda (1901–1966) was a scholar in Buddhist studies. He studied under Zuigan Goto from around 1926 to 1966 and later succeeded him.

Seung-yeon Lee works in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. Supervised by Sang-hae Lee for doctoral studies, Lee held posts at Sungkyunkwan University and the Gyeonggi Institute of Cultural Properties.
